To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) consumers’ willingness-to pay for a specific product is affected by the type of recommendations for other products, and (2) consumers’ willingness to pay is also influenced by the price of the recommended product and the decision stage of the consumer.

the type of recommendation (i.e., complement vs. substitute) has a differential effect on the consumers’ willingness to pay depending on the decision stage, and that the price of a recommendation has a significant main effect on the consumers willingness to pay.

(a) there is no significant effect difference between complement and substitute products in recommendations on consumers’ willingness-to- pay, (b) the interaction effect between the type of recommendations and decision stage is significant, and (c) there are significant main effects of price of the recommended product and the decision stage on consumers’ willingness to pay for the focal product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the effects of complementary and substitute recommendations, and how they interact with the price of a recommendation and the consumer’s decision stage.
the impact of product recommendations on consumers’ economic behavior, which has been largely overlooked in the recommender system literature.
understanding the differential effects of product recommendations on consumers’ willingness-to- pay for the focal product.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of recommendations is dependent on the type of recommendation, the price of the recommendation, and the consumers’ stage in the purchase process.
complementary and substitutable product recommendations have similar effects on the willingness-to-pay of the focal product.

the effect of complementary and substitutive product recommendations on consumers’ willingness-to pay is not significant, and the recommendation price and the consumers' decision stage moderate the effect of recommendations on willingness to pay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the type of recommendations for other products does not have a direct effect on consumers’ willingness-to- pay.
consumers are more willing to pay for a product if the price of the recommended product is high and they are in later stages of the decision process.
the type of recommendation is not the only factor that affects the consumers’ economic behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of complementary and substitute recommendations are not the same.
it is not the type of recommendation that matters, but rather when and how it is presented.
it is important to consider the type of recommendations and consumers’ decision stage in the context of product recommendations.
